findings.title: Agent-authored proposal text is rendered as live HTML with embedded action buttons
findings.summary: Prompt-injection-to-click primitive: proposal text and hold explanations are injected via innerHTML with embedded <button> controls, allowing compromised content to relabel or hide controls

reactions.note: Root cause is missing Go/TypeScript data contract (F6); this is concrete failure mode

findings.section: The service plus a BB plugin
findings.title: State boundary rule violated: 'Autarch holds no state' is already false
findings.summary: Existing code holds state in preferences.json, display.go YAML, and in-process escalate.DecisionQueue. Brainstorm adds five new state items (pins, stamps, glow, alternatives, history) without per-item ownership ruling.

findings.title: Dispatch substrate rewrite not named: Mycroft is tmux-based, not BB-thread-based
findings.summary: Current Mycroft spawns agents via tmux sessions (spawn/spawner.go:33, patrol/source.go), zero BB integration. Brainstorm assumes 'Mycroft coordinates agents as BB threads' without naming this as a rewrite of the dispatch substrate.

reactions.note: Elevates this to threat surface concern—rail approve/override buttons have no verified path to invoke spawning
This is an ordering dependency that precedes T1 dispatch capability

findings.title: Map placement and neglect data insufficient at launch
findings.summary: Map placement data real for only 51/98 gardens; core-doc shelf data for 20/29 named gardens. Most of estate's positions/rings will be fallback or unscanned, undermining map's #1 job (gestalt/spatial memory) and daily-use trust.

findings.title: Two escalation queues with no stated relationship
findings.summary: in-process escalate.DecisionQueue (Go/TUI) vs. BB-plugin rail escalation queue. Two independent queues can silently believe the other has handled an item (Schelling trap), creating unescalated blockers or double-counting escalation load.

reactions.evidence: own finding S3 (no audit trail), S5 (coordinator race)

findings.section: The service plus a BB plugin
findings.title: No data contract between Go service and TypeScript plugin
findings.summary: Go structs that would feed the plugin are not exposed over any wire protocol. Without a schema, there's no defined rule for treating proposal text as untrusted data vs. trusted markup.

reactions.note: S1's injection mechanism is concrete failure mode of this gap; lack of schema means no sanitization rule can be attached

findings.title: T1 approval dispatch scheduled before one-coordinator claim exists
findings.summary: Approval-driven dispatch at T1 is planned before the one-coordinator claim mechanism is built; bbDev/bbOps coordinators already run outside Mycroft's suggestion flow, creating double-dispatch risk at T1, not only autonomous tiers.

reactions.evidence: F2 (dispatch substrate mismatch), F4 (escalation queue ambiguity)

findings.title: No success criteria: 'Earn its space' is aspirational, not measurable
findings.summary: No metrics defined for what 'earn its space' looks like operationally. No graduation test stated between map+rail stage and next phase. Creates risk of accumulating obligations without exit path.

reactions.evidence: F2 (same absence from user flow angle)

findings.title: No kill criterion stated
findings.summary: Document does not state 'if unused by X date, we stop' decision. No pre-committed exit rule for the map+rail feature.

reactions.note: This is evidence of broader hysteresis problem—no exit mechanic at any scale

findings.title: All four map jobs selected with no prioritization
findings.summary: Unfocused scope: attention, allocation, dependencies, neglect lenses selected simultaneously without ranking. Three of four are seasonal concerns, not daily-persistent affordances.

reactions.evidence: F3 (same scope observation from user flow)

findings.title: Mycroft proposals create reinforcing escalation feedback loop
findings.summary: Proposal-approval loop amplifies escalation load on the rail rather than reducing it. Feedback loop lacks balancing mechanism or completion signal.

findings.title: Bootstrap lowers barrier to entry with no balancing mechanism
findings.summary: Bootstrapping new projects from rail removes friction; 'Goodhart's Law on 8/8 docs' creates false signal stability. No estate-size valve; unbounded sprawl risk.

reactions.note: Extends S4 (bootstrap creates resources behind one click) with repetition/rate-limit dimension

findings.title: Neglect fade and glow settle independently; no recovery path for stalled gardens
findings.summary: Neglect signal conflates peaceful steady-state with abandonment. Fade and glow settle without explicit alert or recovery mechanism. Slow-layer gardens become invisible once marked as neglected.

reactions.evidence: UNTOUCHED-001 (thread activity ≠ tending; unstated model produces ambiguity)

findings.title: 47/98 gardens lack ecosystem data
findings.summary: Map will show placement without stating confidence. Missing ecosystem data for half the estate undermines core job (spatial memory) unless confidence signals are added.

findings.title: 5 documented edges vs ~98 gardens
findings.summary: Blast radius and coupling model fundamentally incomplete. Dependency edges missing for 94% of relationships.

findings.title: Thread activity is not a reliable proxy for tending
findings.summary: newer(last_commit, last_thread_activity) is an unstated model of 'visit'. Conflates thread-based work with actual tending. Neglect signal is noisy; quiet steady-state indistinguishable from abandoned.

reactions.evidence: NEGLECT_SIGNAL_DECAY finding grounds this in causal input to ambiguity

sycophancy_analysis.note: All agents engaged substantively; reactions add independent framing or evidence
